status_summary: No executive order or form change adding a First Amendment assurance to SF-424 applications was found. Executive Order 14332 (Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking), signed 2025-08-07, mentions free speech once in its findings but does not name the First Amendment, SF-424 or applicant assurances; it directs OMB to streamline application requirements and revise the Uniform Guidance. On 2026-05-29 OMB published a proposed rule (91 FR 32198) restructuring 2 CFR part 200, which lists a section prohibiting discriminatory event services; a law-firm summary of 2026-07-08 describes that section as barring recipients from discriminating in event services based on the viewpoint or content of speech, a related but different instrument that was not final as of 2026-10-15.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14332, Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking, was signed (published 2025-08-12, 2025-15344); it requires senior appointee review of funding announcements, directs OMB to streamline application requirements and revise the Uniform Guidance, and includes no First Amendment assurance.
OMB, with grantmaking agencies, published a proposed rule, Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (91 FR 32198, docket OMB-2026-0034), with comments due 2026-07-13.

title: Executive order requiring SF-424 grant applications to assure First Amendment compliance
uncertainties: Searches run: one web search by the researcher (SF-424, First Amendment, assurances, OMB Uniform Guidance, executive order on grantmaking) plus Federal Register API queries; the reviewer ran no web search and queried the Federal Register API for the rule's title since 2026-06-01, which returned only regulatory agenda notices and no final rule. The OMB proposed rule page was truncated, so a speech assurance in unread text cannot be excluded; the description of the event-services section comes from a law-firm summary, which says OMB targeted an effective date of 2026-10-01. The SF-424 forms on grants.gov were not inspected. Department grant certifications on DEI are a different subject and were not counted.
